fields.title: The reconciliation reports breaks on refunds issued just before midnight UTC

sections.Symptom:
The daily reconciliation reports breaks on refunds issued between 23:00 and midnight UTC. Each refund breaks twice, with the same PSP reference and the same amount:

* `in file, not in ledger` on the day the PSP settled it
* `in ledger, not in file` on the day after

The breaks appear only while the UK is on British Summer Time, from the last Sunday in March to the last Sunday in October.
sections.Environment: The nightly reconciliation in [svc-payment-ledger](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b559480e9fc59ea8a218340da7a26bbcaf1a92ec/examples/payments/services/payment-ledger.md), run against the PSP's settlement file during British Summer Time.
sections.Cause: The run cuts its day at midnight UK local time, and the PSP cuts its settlement file at midnight UTC. During British Summer Time, local midnight is 23:00 UTC. A refund written to the ledger between 23:00 and midnight UTC falls into the next day's ledger window, and into the current day's settlement file.
sections.Resolution:
1. In `payment-ledger`, change the reconciliation's day boundaries from midnight `Europe/London` to midnight UTC. Build
   the window's start and end as `DateTimeOffset` values at offset zero, and remove the conversion to local time.
2. Rerun the reconciliation for each day since the clocks went forward that reported a break on a refund.
3. Leave the first run's record for each day as it is. [std-RECON](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b559480e9fc59ea8a218340da7a26bbcaf1a92ec/examples/payments/standards/ledger/reconciliation.md) keeps every run's record for seven years, and
   forbids closing a break by editing a run's output.
4. Check that each rerun matches every refund written between 23:00 and midnight UTC, and reports no break for it.
sections.Why it happens:
Every ledger entry written in that hour falls on the wrong side of the cut. Refunds are the entries that show, because a refund follows an accepted return at any hour, and a capture happens only when an order ships.

The run's window and the settlement file agree for the five months the UK spends on UTC, so the fault appears only once the clocks go forward.
